sentences.text: The Ontario SARS Commission concluded that hospital infection control was inadequate throughout Ontario.

A 2000 survey of infection control programs in acute care hospitals in Ontario with more than 80 acute care beds found that 40% of infection control programs had fewer infection control professionals than recommended by SENIC, and 80% did not meet Canadian recommendations.

The survey identified that 12% of acute care hospitals with more than 200 beds had no infection control program, and 40% of Canadian hospitals did not have physicians or doctoral professionals with infection control training who provided service to the infection control program.
The Commission found that infection control failed to protect nurses during SARS.
The Commission noted that many Ontario hospitals are in older buildings whose structure does not lend itself to modern infection control practices.

The Commission recommended that the Ministry of Health ensure that all Ontario hospitals have infection control personnel, resources and program components, including surveillance, control and education, consistent with Canadian standards.

answer.text: The Ontario SARS Commission concluded that hospital infection control was inadequate throughout Ontario. A 2000 survey of infection control programs in acute care hospitals in Ontario with more than 80 acute care beds found that 40% of infection control programs had fewer infection control professionals than recommended by SENIC, and 80% did not meet Canadian recommendations. The survey identified that 12% of acute care hospitals with more than 200 beds had no infection control program, and 40% of Canadian hospitals did not have physicians or doctoral professionals with infection control training who provided service to the infection control program. The Commission found that infection control failed to protect nurses during SARS. The Commission noted that many Ontario hospitals are in older buildings whose structure does not lend itself to modern infection control practices. The Commission recommended that the Ministry of Health ensure that all Ontario hospitals have infection control personnel, resources and program components, including surveillance, control and education, consistent with Canadian standards.
